name: tldr
description: A TL;DR under every long reply: the most important points first, as a plain list, in simple language, for a reader with no time.

min_words.title: Shortest reply that gets a TL;DR
min_words.description: A reply with fewer words of prose than this gets no summary. Code blocks and table rows do not count. 0 summarizes every reply.

max_points.title: Most points in a TL;DR
max_points.description: The summary is a list of at most this many points, the most important first.

model.title: Model that writes the TL;DR
model.description: A full model name. claude-opus-5-5 (the default) answered in about four seconds when measured, claude-sonnet-5-5 in about three, claude-fable-5-1 in four to six; claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 is the cheapest but took seven to forty seconds. It runs through your own claude login, as a nested `claude -p`, and sees only the reply being summarized. Short aliases such as opus or haiku are not accepted by that call.

heading.title: Heading over the summary
heading.description: The line shown above the points.

timeout.title: Seconds to wait for the summary
timeout.description: The nested model call is given this long; past it the reply is shown without a summary. 10 to 120.

instructions.title: Your instructions for the summary
instructions.description: A sentence or a few, added to the plugin's own instructions: for example "Write it in French." or "Say first what I must do next." The format stays a list.

instructions_file.title: A file of instructions for the summary
instructions_file.description: Absolute path to a UTF-8 text file (at most 8 KB), added after the plugin's own instructions and your instructions option. Read at every summary, so an edit takes effect at once.

instructions_mode.title: add or replace
instructions_mode.description: add (the default) keeps the plugin's own instructions and adds yours after them; replace drops the plugin's own, so yours stand alone. A project's .telder.md is always added, and the format rules always apply.
